elements.title: Table 8: De Jure Institutional Autonomy
elements.content:
| Indicator | Vietnam - Regular Public HEIs | Vietnam - Autonomous Public HEIs | Vietnam - Vietnam National Universities | Vietnam - Private Universities | UK | Japan | Estonia | Poland | Malaysia | China |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Determination of student size | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| Decision on opening a new program | 0 | 3 | 3 | 0 | 3 | | 1 | 3 | — | — |
| Decision on course content | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 1 | 3 | 3 | 1 | 1 |
| Selection of Rector/President | 0 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 3 | 3 | 2 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| Recruitment of staff | 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 1 |
| Determination of tuition fee for domestic students | 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Decision on bank interest income/surplus | 0 | 3 | 0 | — | 3 | | 3 | 1 | — | — |

Source: Authors’ estimates based on review of regulations for Vietnam and benchmarking countries.
Note: Scores generated through review of regulations across countries and Vietnam University Autonomy Scorecard and developed based on European University Autonomy Scorecard (Estermann et al. 2011). Institutional autonomy is scored from 0 to 3 in which 0 refers to no autonomy and 3 to full autonomy. Benchmarking countries include those which have advanced higher education systems, some from former Soviet Union and some from the region.
